candidates.lead: Courteeners frontman Liam Fray revisits the Manchester pub where he first got on stage in 2005
candidates.evidence_text: The street outside legendary indie club 42s, a front garden on Burnage Lane and a pub's function room with a tiny stage - all locations in Manchester where you could have found Courteeners in their early days The four school friends from Middleton, near Rochdale, have certainly come a long way since they hit the Manchester indie scene in 2006 But while they have travelled around the word aplenty ever since, there is no place like home, and later they will take to the stage for a huge homecoming gig at Wythenshawe Park From humble beginnings - performing for friends in the garden of their shared house in Burnage - the Courteeners are now celebrating 20 years together Fresh from releasing a new best-of compilation album called God Bless The Band, lead singer and songwriter Liam Fray spoke to BBC North West Tonight at The Briton's Protection pub on Deansgate, where he first performed as a solo artist back in 2005 Sitting upstairs in the pub, Fray smiled at the 3ft (2m) stage and single spotlight on the ceiling while recalling the night he spent there more than two decades ago

candidates.evidence_text: When World War One broke out in 1914, Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner But by the end of 1916, he had enlisted in the Cheshire Regiment of the British Army where he trained as a stretcher bearer to collect the wounded from the battlefields He was then transferred to the 10th Battalion Northumberland Fusiliers where he would later take part in one of the last battles of the World War One involving British soldiers fighting in Italy The Battle of Vittorio Veneto was fought from 24 October to 3 November 1918 and was seen as a decisive victory that contributed to the end of the war Mark Smith, who is a medals specialist at Stanley Gibbons Baldwins, said Wood went above and beyond what was expected of him and used his own initiative when his unit was held up by hostile machine guns and snipers The Stockport shed cleaner given the Victoria Cross

candidates.summary: The track, born from the frontman's car collision in Manchester, concludes he "should've got the 192"

candidates.lead: The track, born from the frontman's car collision in Manchester, concludes he "should've got the 192"
candidates.evidence_text: Blossoms new song about Manchester to Stockport 192 bus route - BBC News Image source, Ewan Ogden Image caption, Stockport indie band Blossoms have released a new single paying homage to the Manchester to Stockport bus route By Georgie Docker North West Published 28 August 2026 Stockport indie band Blossoms has released a new song inspired by Greater Manchester's No. 192 bus. Additional Driver, featuring fellow indie artist Declan McKenna, was born from a minor car collision involving frontman Tom Ogden outside Manchester's O2 Apollo. The song tells the story of a journey from Manchester to Stockport that goes wrong, with the repeated refrain: "Should've got the 192". The accompanying music video was filmed aboard a Bee Network bus, bringing one of Greater Manchester's best-known bus routes into the spotlight. Image source, Ewan Ogden Image caption, The song's music video is shot on the 192 bus - one of the region's best-known routes. "Last year we went writing in Wales and invited Declan," Ogden explains. "I brought up a small bump I had in the car outside the Apollo, the previous week before the session. "A vocal take in the hot tub later we had finished writing what would become 'Additional Driver'. "We knew we wanted to try it out for the album so we invited Declan to Tilehouse when we were recording the album." Image source, Ewan Ogden Image caption, Blossoms have had four number one albums in the UK charts Blossoms are following in the footsteps of other successful indie and rock bands who have found inspiration on Britain's buses. The Clash referenced London's No. 19 bus in Rudie Can't Fail, while Birmingham band Superfood featured the No. 9 route in Unstoppable. Additional Driver tells the story of a journey home that begins when approaching the junction at the O2 Apollo, in Manchester city centre. The song concludes with the closing lines, "Should've got the 192". Ben Gamble, the Stagecoach driver who was behind the wheel of the bus featured in the music video said he "really enjoyed meeting Blossoms". "They are a really good bunch of lads, very polite and chatty," he said. "It was a pleasure to drive them around while they filmed their music video." Image source, TfGM Image caption, The band were named British Breakthrough Act at the Brit Awards in 2017 Transport for Greater Manchester's chief network officer Danny Vaughan, said: "For many people across Greater Manchester, the 192 is more than a bus route. "It's part of daily life and part of the story of growing up, working, studying and socialising in our city-region. "It's brilliant to see a hometown band like Blossoms put the route centre stage and introduce it to audiences beyond Greater Manchester." candidates.lead: Manchester Airport is expecting around half a million passengers this bank holiday
candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Airport warns passengers ahead of busy bank holiday - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, Passengers are being warned not to pack items powered by lithium batteries in hold bags By Haider Saleem Reporting from North West Published 28 August 2026 Passengers travelling through Manchester Airport over the August bank holiday weekend have been warned to check how they pack to help reduce delays during one of the busiest weekends in the airport's history. The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) has urged travellers to avoid packing battery-powered devices in hold luggage as they pose a fire risk. It said bags may have to be offloaded if items such as vapes and power banks are found in them. About two million passengers are expected to depart from airports across Great Britain during the weekend, according to the regulator. 'Catch fire without warning' Anthony Shaw, a security team leader in the airport's hold baggage screening team, said staff often find devices including vapes, power banks and tablets in checked luggage. "If the battery gets too hot, or is faulty, it can catch fire without warning," he said. Shaw said staff could screen almost 1,000 bags for a large long-haul aircraft and several hundred for a short-haul flight. "Each bag that fails to pass security checks gets pulled aside, and often needs to be inspected manually," he said. "This can create delays, but it also creates a risk that your hold bag might not make it onto the plane at all." The CAA said a fire on board could result in an aircraft being diverted or evacuated. Vapes, power banks and spare batteries must be carried in the cabin rather than placed in checked baggage. The CAA advised travellers to check their airline's rules before setting off because additional restrictions may apply. Big name chefs include James Martin, Marco Pierre White and Nisha Katona will serve up cooking demos. The festival site is spread across the town centre and organisers suggest Victoria Square information point is the best place for visitors to collect a free guide to help plan their day. Debbie Newall, Bolton Council's executive cabinet member for culture, said: "This is an opportunity to support local traders, celebrate fantastic food and drink, and showcase the very best of Bolton." "From artisan stalls and celebrity chef demonstrations, to live music and family activities, there is something for everyone to enjoy. "We are so proud of the continued success of the festival, and I urge everyone to visit and show their support." Free events taking place include street performers, children's activities, live music and entertainment throughout the weekend including headliners Liberty X and The Real Thing with demonstrations from regional chefs at Victoria Square. Meanwhile interactive experiences across the festival site include circus skills workshops, giant doodle walls, bubble performances, creative art sessions and a giant sandpit. candidates.evidence_text: Salford to extend long-term home-building plans - BBC News Image caption, Mike McCusker is the council's lead member for planning By Richard Stead North West Published 28 August 2026 Members of the public are being invited to have their say about plans to build nearly 35,000 new homes in Salford over the next 17 years - while also protecting the city's greenery. Extending the council's home-building plans by four years, a new document has sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043. Deputy mayor and planning boss Mike McCusker said: "We will have a brand new development plan, which will give us a good pipeline of new homes as well as protection from developers, who could successfully appeal against planning applications which the council has rejected. "At the same time its important to protect our valuable green spaces for local people." Salford Council's existing local plan, which is part of the Greater Manchester-wide Places For Everyone strategy, outlines sites to be developed until 2039. Image caption, The draft local plan outlines the ambition to build warehouses on empty land next to the Salford Community Stadium The city has been one of the fastest growing in the UK over recent years, with its population rising to 294,000 in 2024 - an increase of 34% since 2001. Most of that growth has been in the city centre - and at Salford Quays - but there have also been new homes built on former green belt land in areas like Boothstown. Councillors will vote on the draft local plan before the end of this year and it will then be submitted to the government for final approval. According to the draft plan, there will be a particular focus on development in the city centre, the Quays, Port Salford, and the site of the Salford Community Stadium. The stadium was fully acquired by the council in December 2024, when it bought Peel Land's 50% stake in the rugby ground for £7.7m. Image caption, Ivan Voronov is the leader of Reform UK on Salford Council The stadium was built in 2012 and the draft plan outlines ambitions for warehouses to be built on the empty surrounding land, supported by a possible Metrolink tram extension to Port Salford. However, Local Reform leader Ivan Voronov said: "The stadium is losing money every single year and we've been throwing good money after bad, so we should be cutting or losses on this. "Elsewhere, there's very little to support local GPs in places like Salford Quays, so how can you build another gigantic new skyscraper and not build any new medical facilities to support that?" Image caption, There are plans for 130 homes on the former St Ambrose Barlow High School site in Swinton The draft plan also includes a scheme for 130 homes on the former St Ambrose Barlow High School site in Swinton, which has been vacant since 2013. Brownfield land, which would be suitable for about 300 houses and 170 apartments, has also been identified off Orchard Street in Pendleton. There are also plans to provide an additional 35 pitches for the travelling community by extending their existing site on Duchy Road in Pendleton. The draft proposals would also give extra protection to 12 local greens, including land at Kersal Moor, Peel Park next to the University of Salford, Brickfield Wood in Boothstown and the Three Sisters nature reserve in Ellesmere Park. But top councillors said there would be no cuts to services as a result of the change From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will be collected every two weeks instead of every four weeks across Stockport . The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025 Earlier this week, councillor Jake Austin, who is the cabinet member overseeing bin services, said he was delighted to announce the move and feedback had been ‘loud and clear’ that people ‘want a service that makes it easier to recycle’ Council leader Mark Roberts said: “It is critical people know the Liberal Democrats will listen to the feedback given and strive to make a positive difference wherever we can.” The announcement this week has come after weeks of criticism of the local authority . Recent controversial enforcement of a long-standing policy around collecting bins with open lids led to hundreds of people being left with uncollected bins

But in the community where those harrowing scenes unfolded, there is a sense that drivers are still refusing to take the risks of the road seriously "I do think it shocked a few people, but it won’t be long before there’s another one," Melissa McCarney said. The 19-year-old was one of a string of residents living close to the crash scene who spoke to the Manchester Evening News this week More than seven months on from the crash, road safety is still a constant source of concern for residents. Neighbours describe having had multiple cars written off over the years, on a street likened to a 'race track'

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig says Tyldesley's giant 'cruise ship' warehouses ‘doesn’t sit right' The 60ft warehouses, yards from homes in Tyldesley, have been likened to cruiseships Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 20:01, 2 Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig has said a controversial giant warehouse development in Tyldesley ‘doesn’t sit right’ with her The mayor met representatives of the Astley Warehouses Action group after a walking around the site. Earlier this summer, logistics firm Whistl started around the clock operations at the controversial ‘cruise ship’ warehouse complex in Tyldesley The development, commissioned by PLP, has been dogged by controversy for more than a year since building work started. Many residents, some of whom have gardens just 30 metres from the 350,000 sq ft logistics site, have criticised the huge scale and appearance of the ‘towering wa Incidents of flooding on nearby paths and gardens have also occurred last winter with complaints that run off from the construction site was causing the issues On a visit to the area, Bev Craig said: “I was really keen to talk to residents, like everyone else I’ve seen the pictures online and it didn’t sit right with me to build something so big so close to residential properties

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Airport EasyJet nightmare as pilot cancels Manchester Airport flight on the runway before replacement ends up 1,290 miles from destination Passengers have been left 'stranded' after a pilot at Manchester Airport suddenly cancelled their fli Hundreds of holiday-goers have been left hit by hours of delays and stuck 1,200 miles from their destination after their flight from Manchester was suddenly cancelled Passengers on the easyJet flight to Antalya this morning, Friday (August 28), say they were told to leave the runway 'ten minutes' before their flight was due to depart. One passenger said they were due to board the plane when they were told to return to the terminal. The airline But following a wait of more than four hours, passengers, who were originally due to depart at 7.45am, eventually took off to their holiday destination at around 12pm after a replacement crew was found, the Manchester Evening News understands However, when in the air, passengers say they were told the flight needed to divert to Milan, as the staff couldn't legally carry on working as the crew had reached its duty-time limit Passengers from the plane, which they said largely consisted of families with young children, were taken to Milan Airport - over 1,200 miles from their destination. They have been given a €25 food voucher while they wait for their new crew to arrive, apparently coming from Manche

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Cowboy builder overpromised, underdelivered and left families 'in a state' He caused £1m of damage - but now he is behind bars News Rachel Smith Court reporter and Stephen Topping Senior reporter 14:12, 28 Aug 2026 View Image Patrick Hartley A cowboy builder who 'overpromised and underdelivered' left damage worth £1m to homes in Greater Manchester and Lancashire . A court heard how Patrick Hartley left homeowners without adequate roofing The 40-year-old would take customers' money before moving on to the next job, leaving work unfinished. His actions put families under strain as they took on more debt to have the work put right, Lancs Live reports The court heard Hartley, from Bacup, Rossendale, stung 13 families in a 30-month period from 2020. His fraudulent activity landed him a prison sentence of three years and nine months Judge Andrew Jeffries KC told him: "Any conscientious builder would simply have stopped. You continued to take on fresh work when the truth was you were leaving jobs incomplete and families in a state." The court heard Hartley was sent written letters and warnings after customers complained about the work. In some cases the builder promised refunds which never came

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport council accused of U-turn after plan to increase bin collections Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 07:42, 29 Aug 2026 View Ima Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ following a major bin announcement. But top councillors said there would be no cuts to services as a result of the change From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will be collected every two weeks instead of every four weeks across Stockport . The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025 Earlier this week, councillor Jake Austin, who is the cabinet member overseeing bin services, said he was delighted to announce the move and feedback had been ‘loud and clear’ that people ‘want a service that makes it easier to recycle’ Council leader Mark Roberts said: “It is critical people know the Liberal Democrats will listen to the feedback given and strive to make a positive difference wherever we can.” The announcement this week has come after weeks of criticism of the local authority . Recent controversial enforcement of a long-standing policy around collecting bins with open lids led to hundreds of people being left with uncollected bins

candidates.summary: Bolton The tragedy they knew was coming Four men were killed in a horrific head-on crash - but on the road where it happened, residents expect another major incident View 9 Images Mohammed Jibrael Mukhtar, Mohammed-Danyaal Asghar-Ali, Farhan Patel and News Stephen Topping Senior

candidates.lead: Bolton The tragedy they knew was coming Four men were killed in a horrific head-on crash - but on the road where it happened, residents expect another major incident View 9 Images Mohammed Jibrael Mukhtar, Mohammed-Danyaal Asghar-Ali, Farhan Patel and News Stephen Topping Senior
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton The tragedy they knew was coming Four men were killed in a horrific head-on crash - but on the road where it happened, residents expect another major incident View 9 Images Mohammed Jibrael Mukhtar, Mohammed-Danyaal Asghar-Ali, Farhan Patel and News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:00, 29 Aug 2026 Updated 07:18, 29 Aug 2026 It was the scene of a devastating tragedy. Four lives lost in a moment. Countless others torn apart Three teenagers and a dad-of-four taxi driver died following a head-on crash on Wigan Road, in Bolton , at 12.45am on Sunday, January 11. Hundreds of people have been left to grieve for their loved ones Those who survived the crash have had to come to terms with horrific injuries . But in the community where those harrowing scenes unfolded, there is a sense that drivers are still refusing to take the risks of the road seriously "I do think it shocked a few people, but it won’t be long before there’s another one," Melissa McCarney said. The 19-year-old was one of a string of residents living close to the crash scene who spoke to the Manchester Evening News this week More than seven months on from the crash, road safety is still a constant source of concern for residents. Neighbours describe having had multiple cars written off over the years, on a street likened to a 'race track'

candidates.evidence_text: Bury The full story of the flashy young drug dealer shot by police as his empire crumbled Officers have now been told they are not under investigation for their conduct View 6 Images Lewis Hanson (Image: GMP) News Paul Britton Reporter 06:00, 29 Aug 2026 Boxed in by police firearms officers in his trendy Cupra car, years of drug dealing on the streets came to a dramatic end for Lewis Hanson. Unbeknown to him, the flashy criminal Hanson had been under surveillance Cops from GMP's Serious and Organised Crime Group watched as he visited a drugs stash house in Radcliffe, Bury, and drove around Radcliffe, Whitefield and Greenmount They saw him make street deals with users - then made their move just after 3pm on May 22, at the junction of Bury New Road and Chestnut Avenue in Whitefield. Hanson, 20, who spent thousands on designer clothes, 'attempted to evade arrest', Greater Manchester Police said this wee The officers involved in what became a firearms operation attempted to stop the Cupra, but the force said Hanson failed to comply and 'attempted to evade capture' In turn, officers discharged a single shot, striking him in the elbow. A sentencing hearing in court was told one of the attending armed officers 'felt compelled to discharge his firearm'

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Heartless Bacup builder showed 13 families 'no mercy' as he pocketed £700,000 and left a trail of devastation The cowboy builder 'showed no mercy' to families across Greater Manchester and Lancashire Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 16:09, 2 The conviction of a cowboy builder has been welcomed by council investigators who described him as 'one of the most prolific, heartless fraudsters that we have come across' Patrick Hartley, 40, 'overpromised and underdelivered' - and left damage worth £1m to homes in Greater Manchester and Lancashire , a court heard Hartley would take customers' money before moving on to the next job, leaving work unfinished and families under strain as they took on more debt to have the work put right Council bosses said he targeted homes in Oldham , Tameside , Sale , Bury , Bolton and Stockport , as well as in Bacup and Rawtenstall. One of his victims included a couple in Bacup, who asked Hartley to build an extension for an elderly relative so they could take her in during h After Hartley was jailed on Friday, Lancashire County Council issued a statement, saying he preyed on people when they were vulnerable for financial gain

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Man, 28, sexually assaulted girl after asking her what 'favours' she would do for him in return for a vape Furqan Khalil assaulted the victim at his mobile phone and e-cigarette shop News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 14:54, 28 Aug 2026 View Image A 28-year-old man from Bolton has been found guilty of sexually assaulting a girl in Northwich. Furqan Khalil assaulted the girl at his mobile phone and e-cigarette shop, asking her what “favours” she would do for him in return for a vape Khalil of Rishton Lane, Bolton , was found guilty of engaging in non-penetrative sexual activity with a child following a four-day trial at Chester Crown Court which concluded on Thursday (August 27) The court heard that in February 2024, the victim entered Khalil’s mobile phone and e-cigarette shop in Northwich to buy a phone charger While in the shop, she asked whether she could purchase a vape. As Khalil showed her a selection, he touched her inappropriately. After she chose a vape, Khalil told her to wait outside, claiming he could not give it to her inside because of the CCTV cameras Once outside, Khalil again touched the victim inappropriately. When she asked for the vape, he instead asked what “favours” she would do for him in return

A court heard how Patrick Hartley left homeowners without adequate roofing The 40-year-old would take customers' money before moving on to the next job, leaving work unfinished. His actions put families under strain as they took on more debt to have the work put right, Lancs Live reports The court heard Hartley, from Bacup, Rossendale, stung 13 families in a 30-month period from 2020. His fraudulent activity landed him a prison sentence of three years and nine months Judge Andrew Jeffries KC told him: "Any conscientious builder would simply have stopped. You continued to take on fresh work when the truth was you were leaving jobs incomplete and families in a state." The court heard Hartley was sent written letters and warnings after customers complained about the work. In some cases the builder promised refunds which never came

Emergency services descended on Stockport Road, in Haughton Green , at around 9.45pm on Thursday evening (August 27) The incident involved a grey Citroen C3, which landed on its roof following the collision with a milk float. Police, firefighters and paramedics all attended the scene A man and a woman were treated by paramedics following the collision. No serious injuries were reported following the crash, according to Greater Manchester Police The force confirmed it was called out to a two-vehicle collision at 9.45pm. candidates.evidence_text: Parklife Festival Seven people arrested in London raids linked to string of Parklife Festival robberies Police say some of the victims were attacked News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 10:55, 28 Aug 2026 Updated 12:09, 28 Aug 2026 Greater Manchester Victims reported being approached in crowded areas of the festival and asked to hand over valuable items, including mobile phones and jewellery. GMP says that in several incidents, those who resisted - or those who had friends that stepped in to help - were subjected to violence Investigators believe members of the group would walk through the crowds and pass the stolen items back and forth, making it difficult to track where they had gone. CCTV footage allowed victims to identify one suspect While being arrested on suspicion of robbery, investigators seized and examined his mobile phone. GMP says officers discovered evidence which indicated a wider criminal network had been in operation Further evidence and intelligence led to a joint operation between GMP and Metropolitan Police, who executed warrants at 12 addresses across London on Wednesday morning (August 26). Seven people were arrested on suspicion of robbery and other related offences View Image It follows a string of incidents at this year's Parklife Festival (Image: Manchester Evening News)

Emergency services descended on Huddersfield Road , in Ashton-under-Lyne , on Thursday afternoon (August 27) Greater Manchester Police says it was called out to a collision at around 2.40pm. It's believed a Toyota Yaris was turning off Huddersfield Road when it hit the pedestrian He was rushed to hospital for treatment, where he remains in a life-threatening conditions this morning (Friday). GMP says the driver remained at the scene of the crash No arrests have been made following the incident. Part of Huddersfield Road remained closed for hours following the incident, while an air ambulance was pictured landing nearby North West Ambulance Service said it 'dispatched several ambulance resources to the scene' including the air ambulance. "A patient has been transported to Salford Royal with a serious head injury," a spokesperson said

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport council accused of U-turn after plan to increase bin collections Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 07:42, 29 Aug 2026 View Ima Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ following a major bin announcement. But top councillors said there would be no cuts to services as a result of the change From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will be collected every two weeks instead of every four weeks across Stockport . The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025 Earlier this week, councillor Jake Austin, who is the cabinet member overseeing bin services, said he was delighted to announce the move and feedback had been ‘loud and clear’ that people ‘want a service that makes it easier to recycle’ Council leader Mark Roberts said: “It is critical people know the Liberal Democrats will listen to the feedback given and strive to make a positive difference wherever we can.” The announcement this week has come after weeks of criticism of the local authority . Recent controversial enforcement of a long-standing policy around collecting bins with open lids led to hundreds of people being left with uncollected bins

The contractors have finished their part in the £40m project, with the council now set to get the ‘final fixtures and fittings’ in place The hub is ‘on track’ to open this autumn, leaders have said. candidates.summary: Bolton The tragedy they knew was coming Four men were killed in a horrific head-on crash - but on the road where it happened, residents expect another major incident View 9 Images Mohammed Jibrael Mukhtar, Mohammed-Danyaal Asghar-Ali, Farhan Patel and News Stephen Topping Senior

candidates.lead: Bolton The tragedy they knew was coming Four men were killed in a horrific head-on crash - but on the road where it happened, residents expect another major incident View 9 Images Mohammed Jibrael Mukhtar, Mohammed-Danyaal Asghar-Ali, Farhan Patel and News Stephen Topping Senior
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton The tragedy they knew was coming Four men were killed in a horrific head-on crash - but on the road where it happened, residents expect another major incident View 9 Images Mohammed Jibrael Mukhtar, Mohammed-Danyaal Asghar-Ali, Farhan Patel and News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:00, 29 Aug 2026 Updated 07:18, 29 Aug 2026 It was the scene of a devastating tragedy. Four lives lost in a moment. Countless others torn apart Three teenagers and a dad-of-four taxi driver died following a head-on crash on Wigan Road, in Bolton , at 12.45am on Sunday, January 11. Hundreds of people have been left to grieve for their loved ones Those who survived the crash have had to come to terms with horrific injuries . But in the community where those harrowing scenes unfolded, there is a sense that drivers are still refusing to take the risks of the road seriously "I do think it shocked a few people, but it won’t be long before there’s another one," Melissa McCarney said. The 19-year-old was one of a string of residents living close to the crash scene who spoke to the Manchester Evening News this week More than seven months on from the crash, road safety is still a constant source of concern for residents. Neighbours describe having had multiple cars written off over the years, on a street likened to a 'race track'

candidates.evidence_text: Crime Youth club worker arrested as police investigate allegations boy was sexually assaulted 'I had a gut feeling that something was not right', the boy's mother said News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:00, 29 Aug 2026 View Image A police investigati Police are investigating allegations a child was sexually assaulted by a staff member at a Greater Manchester youth club The worker has been suspended and detectives have made an arrest. The force was alerted earlier this year when the boy's mother made a complaint She told the Manchester Evening News she fears her son was being groomed. He told her he had been 'hugged and kissed' and 'told to keep things secret', she added In a statement, Greater Manchester Police said: "A man was arrested on suspicion of sexual assault. Enquiries are ongoing." Bosses said in a statement: "We are aware of an ongoing police investigation relating to one of our employees and we are cooperating fully with Greater Manchester Police and the local authority. The safety and wellbeing of young people remains our highest priority."

candidates.evidence_text: Bury The full story of the flashy young drug dealer shot by police as his empire crumbled Officers have now been told they are not under investigation for their conduct View 6 Images Lewis Hanson (Image: GMP) News Paul Britton Reporter 06:00, 29 Aug 2026 Boxed in by police firearms officers in his trendy Cupra car, years of drug dealing on the streets came to a dramatic end for Lewis Hanson. Unbeknown to him, the flashy criminal Hanson had been under surveillance Cops from GMP's Serious and Organised Crime Group watched as he visited a drugs stash house in Radcliffe, Bury, and drove around Radcliffe, Whitefield and Greenmount They saw him make street deals with users - then made their move just after 3pm on May 22, at the junction of Bury New Road and Chestnut Avenue in Whitefield. Hanson, 20, who spent thousands on designer clothes, 'attempted to evade arrest', Greater Manchester Police said this wee The officers involved in what became a firearms operation attempted to stop the Cupra, but the force said Hanson failed to comply and 'attempted to evade capture' In turn, officers discharged a single shot, striking him in the elbow. A sentencing hearing in court was told one of the attending armed officers 'felt compelled to discharge his firearm'

Many residents, some of whom have gardens just 30 metres from the 350,000 sq ft logistics site, have criticised the huge scale and appearance of the ‘towering wa Incidents of flooding on nearby paths and gardens have also occurred last winter with complaints that run off from the construction site was causing the issues On a visit to the area, Bev Craig said: “I was really keen to talk to residents, like everyone else I’ve seen the pictures online and it didn’t sit right with me to build something so big so close to residential properties

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Man City star's £200k Mercedes 'clamped on Manchester back street as he got haircut' Forward Omar Marmoush found his car clamped after parking in a 'loading only' bay Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer and Jam Press 08 A parking howler has reportedly resulted in a Manchester City star's £200,000 car being clamped. 27-year-old star Omar Marmoush was caught out by the council, which left the Egyptian ace with a lock on his wheel and a ticket on his windshield The winger, who signed for City in January 2025 for £59m, had parked his 2025 Mercedes-Benz AMG G 63 MHEV down a back street in the city centre while he got a haircut, according to reports A swish £200,000 motor was spotted with the clamp on South King Street , Manchester The vehicle was spotted in a ‘loading only’ bay on Aug 14 around 8.30 pm. Manchester City Council’s removal fee for a clamp can reach up to £105 if the owner fails to contact them within 24 hours The car will then be towed to the pound where the owner will be charged £12 a day until the vehicle is collected. New research reveals a dramatic rise in youngsters ending News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 14:34, 28 Aug 2026 Updated 15:18, 28 Aug 2026 Doctors treating injured children say there is a dangerous misconception amid the growing popularity of e-scooters Medics in Greater Manchester say they are seeing "several" e-scooter incidents every week. Youngsters have been left with with devastating brain injuries. Sew research reveals the scale of the problem hitting hospitals "We obviously see a lot of minor injuries, which are ankle injuries and upper limb injuries," Caroline Rushmer, children's major trauma coordinator at Royal Manchester Children's Hospital told the Manchester Evening News "But we're also seeing really significant injuries. In some cases, life-altering injuries as a result of using e-scooters." Caroline recalled the case of one boy who crashed after hitting a pothole hidden beneath fallen leaves. Another child, aged just seven, suffered a serious leg break after twisting the throttle on a friend's e-scooter without realising what it did

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Man, 28, sexually assaulted girl after asking her what 'favours' she would do for him in return for a vape Furqan Khalil assaulted the victim at his mobile phone and e-cigarette shop News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 14:54, 28 Aug 2026 View Image A 28-year-old man from Bolton has been found guilty of sexually assaulting a girl in Northwich. Furqan Khalil assaulted the girl at his mobile phone and e-cigarette shop, asking her what “favours” she would do for him in return for a vape Khalil of Rishton Lane, Bolton , was found guilty of engaging in non-penetrative sexual activity with a child following a four-day trial at Chester Crown Court which concluded on Thursday (August 27) The court heard that in February 2024, the victim entered Khalil’s mobile phone and e-cigarette shop in Northwich to buy a phone charger While in the shop, she asked whether she could purchase a vape. As Khalil showed her a selection, he touched her inappropriately. After she chose a vape, Khalil told her to wait outside, claiming he could not give it to her inside because of the CCTV cameras Once outside, Khalil again touched the victim inappropriately. When she asked for the vape, he instead asked what “favours” she would do for him in return

candidates.evidence_text: Parklife Festival Seven people arrested in London raids linked to string of Parklife Festival robberies Police say some of the victims were attacked News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 10:55, 28 Aug 2026 Updated 12:09, 28 Aug 2026 Greater Manchester Victims reported being approached in crowded areas of the festival and asked to hand over valuable items, including mobile phones and jewellery. GMP says that in several incidents, those who resisted - or those who had friends that stepped in to help - were subjected to violence Investigators believe members of the group would walk through the crowds and pass the stolen items back and forth, making it difficult to track where they had gone. CCTV footage allowed victims to identify one suspect While being arrested on suspicion of robbery, investigators seized and examined his mobile phone. GMP says officers discovered evidence which indicated a wider criminal network had been in operation Further evidence and intelligence led to a joint operation between GMP and Metropolitan Police, who executed warrants at 12 addresses across London on Wednesday morning (August 26). Seven people were arrested on suspicion of robbery and other related offences View Image It follows a string of incidents at this year's Parklife Festival (Image: Manchester Evening News)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Changes to former Bolton NatWest bank ordered to be torn down after being built without permission Planning enforcement has been instigated at a former NatWest building which dates back to Victorian times Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy Metal shutters and an extension built without planning permission at a former bank have been ordered to be ripped down In the past few months three metal lean-to shutters have been installed along the side of the former NatWest building on the corner of Church Street, Farnworth, along with an extension. Bolton council has said no planning permission was previously applied for or approved for the The enforcement notice, published by the council, states that subject to any appeal being lodged, the unauthorised extension must be demolished and the roller shutter doors must be removed within two months of notice taking effect on September 30 A third condition of the enforcement notice states: “Restore the south principal elevation of the building to its condition immediately before the unauthorised development took place “This includes but is not limited to, the repair of the original elevation removed or damaged during the construction works using materials to match the original building in appearance, colour, texture and finish.”

I'll be going in first thing. I'll be sitting down with the staff. I'll be setting out my plan for what we're going to achieve "And hopefully people will see that, in week one, I reach the end of that week with some clear announcements of when - not if - I'm going to do some of the things I said I would."

candidates.lead: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway.
candidates.evidence_text: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

Three major retail brands have chosen Manchester’s King Street for landmark new openings in recent months, with Loake, Creed and Aristocracy London all investing in the destination.. . The announcements come as DTZ Investors continues its long-term vision to establish King Street as one of the UK’s leading premium retail and lifestyle destinations.. . Together, the three arrivals reflect King Street’s continued evolution, strengthening its mix of luxury retail and reinforcing its growing appeal to brands seeking distinctive, experience-led locations.. . British footwear brand, Loake, recently opened its first company-owned Manchester store on King Street, bringing a new flagship concept to the city in a 1,542 sq ft space.. . Designed entirely by the brand, the expanded space showcases Loake’s complete product offering in a more immersive retail environment, giving customers access to its widest collection in Manchester.. . Luxury fragrance house Creed also selected King Street for its first standalone boutique outside London, marking a significant milestone in the brand’s UK expansion. The 525 sq ft boutique introduces Creed’s signature fragrance discovery experience to Manchester, with personalised consultations, private appointments, and bespoke services at the heart of the customer journey. Creed agreed to a 10-year lease.. . Earlier this year, luxury menswear atelier, Aristocracy London, chose King Street for its first venture beyond the capital, opening a 4,500 sq ft, three-storey showroom and atelier offering appointment-only styling, ready-to-wear collections, and made-to-measure tailoring.. . Sarah O’Brien, DTZ Investors, said: “The arrival of Loake, Creed, and Aristocracy reflects the continued confidence premium brands have in King Street. Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment The site was vacated later that day. A significant amount of waste was left behind, which has now been removed by the Council’s cleansing team

candidates.lead: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture
candidates.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture From theatre, film and music to a new mural and giant fuzzy felt artwork, the projects cover a wide range of art forms and celebrate Oldham’s people, places and stories Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up . Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. Isobel and Fay will reimagine it for today using patchwork and running-stitch embroidery Local people will be invited to add buildings and places that are important to them, using old clothes and fabric from home

candidates.evidence_text: A new strategy aims to help everyone in Bolton live a healthy, connected and fulfilling life, supported by strong communities, active environments and quality homes The Joint Local Health and Wellbeing (JHWS) Strategy 2026–2029 sets out how organisations across the borough will work together to improve health and wellbeing and reduce health inequalities The strategy has been approved by Bolton's Health and Wellbeing Board, which brings together leaders from local government, public health, social care, the NHS, housing, the voluntary and community sector, and other key partners The strategy places a strong emphasis on prevention, recognising that helping people stay healthy is just as important as treating illness when it occurs It provides a shared framework for partners to take collective action on the factors that have the biggest impact on people's health and wellbeing The Health and Wellbeing Board has identified three priorities where its collective leadership can add the greatest value

evidence_packet.summary: An urgent plea for improved transport links for Leigh has been backed by members of Wigan Council It means Wigan Council will ask Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) and the new Mayor of Greater Manchester to consider ‘interim rapid transport systems’ while long term solution
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An urgent plea for improved transport links for Leigh has been backed by members of Wigan Council It means Wigan Council will ask Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) and the new Mayor of Greater Manchester to consider ‘interim rapid transport systems’ while long term solutions – such as Metrolink – are assessed Councillor Cunliffe, told colleagues improvements are a “matter of urgency” for residents in and around Leigh, with higher frequency for existing services and smaller scale infrastructure projects required He said: “I know as being part of the Mayoral Development Zone things are happening to see about transport improvement and a feasibility study at getting Metrolink into Leigh. I welcome that “But big infrastructure projects can take years. There are things that can be done in the interim period and that is what we would like to explore.” He added that increased travel times into locations in Manchester city centre and surrounding areas leave residents socially excluded, causing “barriers to employment, education, and social mobility”

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. candidates.evidence_text: Grub on the Docks - Media City UK Street Food Line-Up: Featuring Sizzling Seoul, Dukes Po Boys, and more Grub on the Docks Venue Gardens Dates 28 th May - 20 th Sep '26 Open Tuesday to Sunday weekly, 12 noon – 10pm GRUB on the Docks is bringing the flavour this summer – think unreal street food, ice-cold drinks and non-stop vibes right in the MediaCity gardens, on the waterfront. We’re talking a stacked rotation of indie food like Sizzling Seoul, Umami Cartel, Oppa Korean Dogs and more, switching it up every week so there’s always something new to try. NEW challenge, take on the BELLY BUSTER CHALLENGE from CAFF – sausage. bacon. egg. black pudding. hash brown. All packed into one proper Belly Buster bap for £7.50. Time to beat is 5 minutes set the fastest finishing time and your next Belly Buster is FREE . EVENTS Wine on the Docks Every Wednesday | All day, venue hours Midweek just got better. Every Wednesday, buy two glasses of the same wine and we’ll top up the rest of the bottle on us. No catch, no fuss just a proper reason to make Wednesday your new favourite day. Sunset Sessions Every Friday | 5–8pm Clock off and head straight to the water’s edge. A rotating line-up of DJs kicks off the weekend early, with a trader special and a featured drinks offer to match. Same time, same spot, every Friday, your after-work wind-down sorted. Paws on the Docks 8 AUGUST | 22 AUGUST | 5 SEPTEMBER | 19 SEPTEMBER | Mornings Bring the dog, grab a coffee, make a morning of it. Paws on the Docks is our relaxed dog-friendly social – think breakfast specials, water bowls, complimentary pup cups and market stalls that welcome four-legged visitors as warmly as the two-legged ones. Residents social Thursday 20th August – 5pm to 7pm An evening for all MediaCity residents, with a DJ playing live on the docks. A nice informal social, come down, grab a drink and meet other residents at our waterfront setting. Media Makers Mixer Thursday 27th August – 5pm to 7pm A regular hosted networking event for MediaCity’s creative and production community, designed to bring people together and encourage connections across the area. Be the first in the know Sign up to receive email updates on the latest events, news and offers at MediaCity Visit our privacy policy here. Meet Surinder, sweet, strong, and stuck in a never-ending chore list thanks to her two Insta-fame obsessed stepsisters, Lovely and Bubbly. Her only real support? It already has a strong tech base and devolution gives us a chance to align policy, funding and delivery more closely with what is happening on the ground To do that well, Combined Authorities and others need to understand that ecosystems are much broader and deeper than most public-facing institutions realise, that matters if they are going to make good decisions on skills, infrastructure, procurement and innovation support AI and emerging technologies clearly need focus because their impact will be felt across every part of the economy, but policy needs to keep pace with how those technologies are being used by businesses. Government and Combined Authorities will have more impact if they understand The new Digital Campus in Manchester is a good example of where this could become practical; a larger concentration of public sector digital capability in Manchester should create new routes for startups and scaleups to work with the government. candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City & PUMA break ground with ‘AI first’ Posted on August 28, 2026 by staff Manchester City & PUMA break ground with ‘AI first’ Club’s 2026/27 third kit marks first time in professional football that a fan has designed a kit using AI tools Share: SportTech Retail Manchester City & PUMA have announced an ‘AI first’ with the reveal of the club’s 2026/27 third kit. It marks the first time in professional football that a fan has designed a kit using AI tools. PUMA AI Creator is a custom generative AI tool that turns written prompts into kit designs within seconds – with no design experience required. Fans from over 200 countries brought forward their vision for what the third kit should look like, resulting in over 180,000 unique shirts. Following 1.7 million platform ratings, the most popular kits were shortlisted to the final 10, which went to fan vote in January 2025. With votes having been submitted by the club’s global fanbase, the winner was crowned: a white base split by a central two-tone sash, half sky blue, half navy, running the length of the shirt with a subtle gradient effect that shifts as it catches the light. Behind the winning kit was lifelong City fan Elliott. “City has been part of my life for as long as I can remember, so to have designed a kit that will now be worn by the players is a genuine honour,” he said. “I’ve always loved football shirts and design, and I created mine using PUMA AI Creator on my lunch break, never imagining it could actually become a City kit. “The whole experience has been incredible, from seeing people react to the design, to seeing it on the players for the first time when I was invited to the kit shoot. It still feels surreal to know I’ve played a small part in the club’s history, and I hope it becomes a kit that City fans love and look back on for years to come.” Bradford City’s Dashe deal ‘a first in English football’ Dominique Gathier, vice president teamsport, PUMA, said: “PUMA AI Creator represents a genuinely new way of thinking about how football kits are made and who gets to shape them. candidates.evidence_text: Atom Bank CEO expected to step down after ‘failed sale’ Posted on August 28, 2026 by Jonathan Symcox Atom Bank CEO expected to step down after ‘failed sale’ Following reports that co-founder Mark Mullen to be replaced, Newcastle-based neobank confirms “accelerated” succession planning Share: Founders Appointments FinTech Founder 250 The CEO and co-founder of Atom Bank seems set to be replaced in the coming weeks. Mark Mullen co-founded Atom as Britain’s first digital-only bank with Metro Bank founder Anthony Thomson in 2014. Thomson stepped down as chairman in 2018 and Mullen was featured on our Founder 250 list this year . Following what it called ‘pre-IPO’ funding rounds in previous years, this summer the North East firm worked with advisers at Jefferies on a sale process which attracted interest from several private equity firms and at least two building societies. It had hoped that the auction would value it between £600m and £1 billion, but no firm bids were received and it was abandoned in June. Sky News reported that Mullen is expected to be replaced on an interim basis by Andrew Marshall, the company’s CFO. In a statement, the company responded: “In response to recent press news coverage, Atom confirms ongoing discussions between the CEO and board about succession planning and future senior leadership of the executive committee have accelerated in recent weeks. “This is part of the founding CEO and board’s prudent long term planning for Atom’s next stage of growth and development. A further announcement will be made, if appropriate, in due course.” Fund managers fight for control of £1bn UK Scale-up Fund An advocate for the four-day working week, Mullen moved Atom’s headquarters from Durham to Newcastle last year. The bank has 250,000 customers and a substantial presence in the mortgage and savings markets. However its peers such as Revolut and Monzo have built customer bases in the tens of millions in a similar timeframe. Atom employs around 600 people and its shareholders include BBVA, Toscafund and Infinity Investment Partners. It claims to be the UK’s highest rated bank on Trustpilot. candidates.lead: Global operations system SafetyCulture is celebrating 10 years of business in Manchester with the biggest transformation in its history, including a rebrand and new AI capabilities.
candidates.evidence_text: SafetyCulture marks 10 years in Manchester with Mitti rebrand and new AI capabilities - Invest Manchester Skip to main content Skip to footer Digital, cyber & AI SafetyCulture marks 10 years in Manchester with Mitti rebrand and new AI capabilities Published on August 21, 2026 News Global operations system SafetyCulture is celebrating 10 years of business in Manchester with the biggest transformation in its history, including a rebrand and new AI capabilities. SafetyCulture today rebrands as Mitti, a new identity signalling its expansion beyond traditional safety management to an all-in-one operations system for the frontline. The word Mitti means “middle” — the centre of an operation, where decisions get made, and work happens. The platform connects the people on the frontline with those making decisions in the boardroom. After launching in Manchester in 2016, Mitti expanded into a 10,000 sq ft office at Bond on Mosley Street in 2024 as its EMEA headquarters. During the decade, Mitti has built a UK customer base of 18,000 organisations, including Unilever, DHL, H&M, Domino’s Pizza, and Network Rail. Celebrating the milestone, Dawid Jaworski, EMEA Lead at Mitti, says : “Ten years ago we were a handful of people in a small Manchester office trying to convince businesses that the clipboard had had its day. A decade on, this city is the base from which we serve the entire EMEA region. “The customers we serve are the industries this region was built on. That proximity matters. Being surrounded by it keeps us honest about who we’re building for. “The city has grown up alongside us. Manchester is now the UK’s largest tech economy outside London with more than 10,000 tech businesses operating here. We built our first decade in Manchester, and we’re building the next one here too.” The platform is used by the workers who don’t sit at a desk — 80%¹ of the world’s workforce — across manufacturing, construction, retail, quick-service restaurants (QSR), energy and other industries. Among its North West customers is Bury-headquartered structural steelwork firm William Hare, which has completed more than 180,000 inspections on the platform, saved over a million sheets of paper, and standardised more than 500 templates across its sites while remaining audit-ready. The rebrand lands as UK operators face a tightening compliance picture. Martyn’s Law will require premises with a capacity of 200 or more to document emergency procedures and train staff accordingly, with enforcement expected from spring 2027. In construction, the Building Safety Act has raised the bar on inspection records, contractor oversight and evidence trails. Jaworski adds : “Every day, more than 3.4 million images and 380,000 inspections are added to our platform — captured by people on site, mid-shift, doing the actual work. That’s ground truth others can’t replicate. It’s the difference between software that guesses what’s happening on the frontline and software that knows.” The tools meant to help teams meet these obligations are falling short, according to Mitti. Only around one-third of frontline supervisors find their digital tools “very effective,” 2 according to a commissioned study conducted by Forrester Consulting on behalf of Mitti. Central to the new Mitti platform is its ‘5 Star Benchmarking’ capability, which turns years of operational history into one clear score for multi-site operators, showing how each location is performing and, more importantly, how to improve. The platform’s new AI capabilities are built on that same frontline data. Agents gather intelligence and automate processes; AI Assistant surfaces patterns and risks, compares performance against relevant standards and regulations, creates action plans and answers questions in seconds. And AI Issue Creation turns a photo, prompt or voice note into a ready-to-review issue. From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.evidence_text: Football Kai Rooney Michael Owen instantly shot down by Man United legend Wayne Rooney over question about Kai Michael Owen and Wayne Rooney discussed the United icon's son, Kai, in Owen's new documentary Comments Sport Chris Burns Senior Sports Writer 06:00, 29 Aug 2026 Vi Former Manchester United striker Michael Owen has asked Wayne Rooney – the father of United starlet Kai – if he would ever double up as his son's agent – and he received a clear response. The interaction can be seen on Meet the Owens , which premiered on Amazon this week The new show gives insight into the private lives of Owen, his wife Louise, and their four children, Gemma, James, Emily, and Jessica. In the clip, the former England duo discuss their son's forays into professional football after a taping of the Wayne Rooney Show However, the elder Rooney shot down his former team-mate, simply saying, "No, no," and laughing at Owen's suggestion. Kai has signed a scholarship deal at Old Trafford , having been part of United's youth ranks since the age of 11 Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News! As for an agency, the young striker has actually signed with Triple S Sports Management, the same company his father was signed to. The global agency is owned by Rooney Snr's agent, Paul Stretford

candidates.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC I handed back my Man United shirt number – someone else deserved it more This Manchester United hero opted to hand back the iconic shirt number he was given Comments Sport Fasika Zelealem 04:00, 29 Aug 2026 View 3 Images Antonio Valencia wore t Antonio Valencia gave back the iconic No. 7 shirt at Manchester United because he felt another player deserved it more The former United captain spent a decade at Old Trafford and wore his usual No. 25 for nine of those years. After wearing his signature number for three seasons, the ex-Ecuador international became the latest recipient of the famous No. 7 shirt following Michael Owen's departure The number is the most iconic of its kind at United, with the likes of George Best, Bryan Robson, Eric Cantona, David Beckham and Cristiano Ronaldo having worn it. Valencia joined that legendary list of players in the 2012/13 campaign, which remains the last season United won the Despite the title success Valencia enjoyed while wearing it, he ended up reverting to his previous number and admitted he wanted to leave the No. 7 to someone more deserving "Firstly, I would like to thank Sir Alex Ferguson for trusting me with the number seven shirt, because that shirt number has a lot of meaning at Manchester United," Valencia told Seven, powered by Ladbrokes

The Blues are not expected to sign a right-back, but were missing Matheus Nunes for the trip to Selhurst Park. Nunes pulled up with an issue in the warm-up in the Community Shield but looked good off the bench against Bournemouth last week

The Everton manager In contrast to the Everton chief executive, Angus Kinnear, who recently claimed the club were planning to challenge for Europe this season, Moyes insisted the squad needs “a lot of work” before it can achieve that target City have yet to bid for Ndiaye, who has three years remaining on his Everton contract but declined several offers of an extension last season as they did not include a release clause for a Champions League club. “I think it would be very difficult to get it reinvested if anythin On Ndiaye, he added: “I’m certainly not encouraging a bid. I’m not encouraging that in a million years. I don’t know if it would be too tight for time. Deals and contracts are taking much longer now. There seems to be a lot more involved.” Everton remain interested in City’s Jack Grealish, who spent last season on loan at Hill Dickinson Stadium, but a right-back and centre-forward are more of a priority. Moyes added: “I’m saying there’s not much time but I’ll still try to see what we can do. candidates.evidence_text: 17 октября 2026 года в Brixton Jamm состоится концерт Наталки Карпы в Лондоне В Лондоне прозвучит украинская песня, и снова найдет своих людей, ведь на сцену выйдет Наталка Карпа — певица, чей голос уже более двух десятилетий остается голосом света и искренней любви к родной земле. Для многих украинцев за границей ее концерт станет не только художественным Наталья Карпа получила два высших образования, однако именно музыка стала делом ее жизни. От первых фестивалей и конкурсов до больших сцен Украины и мира, от песни “Калина”, открывшей ей путь к широкому признанию, до многочисленных сольных концертов и международных туров для укра Заслуженная артистка Украины, автор десятков популярных композиций, продюсер и общественный деятель в своем репертуаре легко сочетает лирическую нежность и праздничную энергию, а рядом с хорошо известными хитами непременно звучат новые композиции. Недаром поклонники после концерт В Лондоне прозвучат песни, сопровождавшие разные поколения украинцев, будут звучать слова, в которых живут любовь, вера и несокрушимость. Музыка преодолевает расстояния, находит дорогу к сердцу независимо от того, где человек живет сегодня, и оставляет после себя огонь жизни! Чтобы попасть на концерт Наталки Карпы в Лондоне, покупайте билеты на нашем сайте и в кассах города. Еще больше концертов в афише Лондона ищите у нас на сайте

Its approach is rooted in tradition but interpreted through a contemporary lens – cr At the heart of Coco Tang is a belief that Vietnamese hospitality extends far beyond food, with the experience beginning with the first coffee of the day and continuing through to the final cocktail of the night. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
